## Empirical Summary {#sec-empirical-summary}

The experiments reveal a consistent pattern: **DGPs outperform single-layer GPs only when the target function has genuinely non-stationary, compositional structure**.

On the Kin8nm robot kinematics benchmark, DSVGP-2L achieved a 10.7% RMSE reduction over SVGP (0.0699 vs 0.0783) at full scale — the dataset where deeper architectures provided a clear performance advantage. The target is a composition of trigonometric functions, precisely the hierarchical non-linearity where intermediate representations add value. On the financial classification task, where credit-default surfaces are likely more smooth and monotonic, DGPs matched but did not meaningfully exceed single-layer GP performance, confirming that a single RBF kernel is sufficient for this task.

Across the evaluated datasets, the GP family delivered substantially better probability calibration than classical baselines on credit-risk classification. On the credit card dataset (22.1% default rate), GP models achieved 5–13$\times$ lower ECE than XGBoost, confirming the practical value of Bayesian uncertainty quantification where PD estimates must track observed frequencies.

The scaling analysis yields two practical guidelines. First, SVGP is the most data-efficient GP variant: it leads or matches DGPs at small scale ($N < 1{,}000$) across the experiments. Second, additional depth beyond two layers consistently degrades performance — DSVGP-3L collapsed to near-constant predictions at small scale (R² = 0.002 on Kin8nm) and never outperformed DSVGP-2L at any scale, while costing 3–4$\times$ more training time.

For practitioners, the implication is that DGPs warrant consideration when the application domain exhibits known compositional structure (robotics, sensor fusion, multi-stage physical processes) and sufficient data is available ($N > 3{,}000$). For smooth risk surfaces typical of credit and financial modelling, single-layer SVGPs provide comparable discriminative power at lower computational cost and with the same calibration benefits.
